newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania says will do more to lure in foreign cash.
newsitem.headline: Albania says will do more to lure in foreign cash.

text.p: Albania's government pledged on Saturday to step up its efforts to attract more foreign cash to fuel economic revival in Europe's poorest country.

"The government (is) determined to continue backing business and foreign investment, and to improve political and macroeconomic stability," Selim Belortaja, secretary of state for trade, told an international investment conference.
Albania, where communism was toppled in 1990, has attracted a meagre $230 million in foreign investment over the past five years, official figures show.
Belortaja said Albania offered a safe legal framework and strong institutions to support foreign investors, but admitted there was room to improve conditions further.
"We should continue with more speed to clarify property and privatisation issues and the establishment of a more complete banking infrastructure," he said.

About 2,000 foreign companies are operating in the tiny Balkan nation, many of them as joint-ventures with local businesses in such sectors as construction, textiles, food processing and wood processing.

International experts attending the conference agreed the flow of money from abroad was too small, adding the government should concentrate on providing better macroeconomic stability to lure in foreign investment.

"The country needs to consolidate its economic stability. Inflation is not the best way to create incentives to save, or to attract foreign investment," Carlos Elbirt, the World Bank's local representative, told the conference.
Elbirt warned inflation may rise to an annual 20 percent by the end of the year, from six percent last year. As recently as four years ago, inflation was running at 300 percent.
